items.why: The report notes that G and 2D 'both soften monotonically with power' and broaden, and that the Si line hardly moves ('+0.05 +- 0.03 cm-1'). It never concludes that this points to heating, though: it says the 'three sequential spectra cannot separate a real tensile strain from laser heating.'
It converts only the 5 mW shift ('about 116 K (G) and 151 K (2D) above 0.5 mW'), gives no estimate for 2 mW, and adds 'I cannot say whether that is physical.'

It finds a slope of 2.8 that is 'closest to the uniaxial-strain line' (Lee 2.2), alongside the Calizo thermal ratio of 2.1, and says 'the ratio alone does not separate heating from strain.' It never states that a naive vector analysis would misread heating as strain.
It says to 'Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for absolute positions... Use the 2 and 5 mW spectra only to track the power trend,' and it gives a zero-power extrapolation.

It asks for 'laser power at the sample..., the objective NA and spot size' and suggests more power points (0.5–5 mW). It does not suggest measuring below 0.5 mW to check that this spectrum is free of heating.

It uses the 0.5 mW spectrum (G 1581.14, 2D 2669.32 cm-1) as the reference and finds it 'close to the strain-free, undoped reference', noting that the 2D conversion to 532 nm is only rough because the 'dispersion coefficient is approximate'.

wrong_claims.why: Doping is explicitly rejected. Strain is offered only as a reading 'confounded with laser heating', so it is not asserted as the cause.
The report recommends the 0.5 mW spectrum, not the highest-power one.
